detailed_rationale: Oil India (OIL) is a Government-of-India upstream E&P major (crude oil + natural gas production, primarily Assam/Northeast basins, plus a pipeline-transportation segment) that also consolidates Numaligarh Refinery Ltd (NRL), a ~69%-owned refining subsidiary being expanded from 3 to 9 MMTPA. [DATA] Quant panel: final_score_3y 42.12 (borderline-Hold zone), final_score_1y 36.34 (Sell), recommendation_overall Sell; ROE 17.4%, ROCE 16.4%, D/E 0.65, interest coverage 8.7x, PE (trailing) 10.55x, revenue_cagr_3y -2.02% (i.e. shrinking top line over 3 years), revenue_growth_1y +4.4%, bs_flag/liquidity_flag GREEN, 12m return +2.1% but 3m -9.0% and 24m -9.3% (source: full750_scored.csv). [DATA] FY26 (year to Mar-2026): standalone PAT fell 27% YoY to Rs 4,455 cr (from Rs 6,114 cr) as the crude-oil segment's profit-before-tax dropped from Rs 6,073 cr to Rs 4,301 cr on a weaker realised crude price (~$69/bbl per the Q4 concall, down from prior year) partly capped by the windfall-tax (SAED) mechanism, which structurally claws back upside whenever global crude rallies. Natural-gas segment profit also declined YoY. Pipeline-transportation swung to a Rs 392 cr profit from a small loss. Consolidated PAT still rose 7% YoY to Rs 7,551 cr, but this was carried almost entirely by NRL, whose PAT nearly doubled (+90% YoY to Rs 3,057 cr) on a strong GRM of $13.43/bbl -- refining margins are among the most volatile line items in the energy complex and this tailwind is not a repeatable structural driver. (Sources: psuwatch.com FY26 result coverage, scanx.trade FY26 PAT summary.) [DATA] Q4 FY26 (Mar-2026 quarter) consolidated PAT jumped 62% YoY to Rs 2,424 cr on a 5% rise in crude realisation (to $77.89/bbl) and a decade-high daily crude output (10,566 MT) -- a genuinely strong print. [DATA] Q3 FY26 (Dec-2025) was the soft quarter: consolidated PAT fell YoY (reported variously as Rs 1,195-1,429 cr vs Rs 1,339-2,016 cr a year earlier depending on source) on crude-realisation weakness; the board still raised the interim dividend to Rs 7/share (business-standard.com, angelone.in, enersidermedia.com). [DATA] Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter) has NOT yet been reported as of this writing (21-Jul-2026) -- results are due around 31-Jul-2026 per the sector cadence; this call is therefore built on FY26 + Q4 FY26 + Q3 FY26, the latest PIT-available prints, with the freshest quarter still pending. [DATA] Management guidance (Q4 FY26 concall, arthneeti.com): upstream production target of 10-12 MMTOE by FY30 (from 8.7 MMTOE in FY26, a mid-single-digit annualised volume CAGR); gas output targeted to rise from ~8 to 13-15 MMSCMD via 15-18 new pure-gas wells; drilling activity stepped up 35% (74 wells in FY26 to 100 planned in FY27); Reserve Replacement Ratio improved to 1.20x in FY26 from 0.94x in FY25 (a genuine positive -- reserves are being replaced faster than produced); NRL refining capacity expansion 3->9 MMTPA underway; renewables commitment of Rs 20,000 cr toward 5+ GW by 2040 (long-dated, immaterial to the 3-5y earnings window); and a committed $1.8bn stake in the Mozambique LNG (Area 1) project with an additional ~$300mn cost escalation pending Cabinet approval -- a foreign asset in a project with a well-documented history of security-driven delays (Cabo Delgado insurgency forced the operator's multi-year force majeure), which is a real, quant-invisible execution/counterparty risk sitting inside the capex plan.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score is Sell, driven mostly by the 1y momentum/ownership-flow composite (growth_1y_score 22.2, accumulation_1y_score 9.1, ownership_flow_1y -0.26) rather than by a collapse in fundamental quality. Profitability (ROE 17.4%, ROCE 16.4%), leverage (D/E 0.65, interest cover 8.7x), and balance-sheet/liquidity flags (GREEN/GREEN) all remain solid, the multiple is undemanding (10.55x trailing PE, value_score 61.2), reserve replacement is improving (RRR 1.20x), and consolidated earnings actually grew in FY26 (PAT +7%, Q4 +62% YoY) even though the underlying story is more mixed than the headline. I am rescuing this from the quant Sell to Hold: a PSU E&P name at ~10.5x trailing earnings with double-digit ROE/ROCE, a GREEN balance sheet, and a still-growing consolidated bottom line does not clear my bar for an outright Sell just because 3-6 month price momentum has been soft. I am stopping at Hold, not pushing further, because two genuine fundamental concerns keep this from being a buy-the-dip rescue: (1) the FY26 consolidated growth was carried almost entirely by NRL's refining-margin windfall while the core standalone E&P segment (crude PBT -29% YoY) actually weakened, and 3-year revenue CAGR is negative (-2.0%) -- so the 'growth' the quant panel is scoring on the 1y print is largely a cyclical refining-margin one-off riding on top of a shrinking core business; and (2) the windfall/SAED tax mechanism structurally caps OIL's torque to rising crude prices, meaning the obvious bull catalyst (a crude rally) will not flow through to standalone profit the way it would for an unregulated E&P name. Net: fundamentally sound, cheap, cash-generative PSU: Hold, not Sell, but not a name to chase.
summary: Oil India is a profitable, cheaply-valued state-run oil & gas producer (about 10.5x trailing earnings, 17%+ return on equity, manageable debt) whose FY26 consolidated profit grew 7% -- but that growth was carried almost entirely by its refining subsidiary Numaligarh Refinery's unusually strong margins, while Oil India's own core crude-oil business actually saw profit fall roughly 29% for the year on a weaker realised oil price and India's windfall-tax mechanism, which caps how much of any oil-price rally producers get to keep. Reserves are being replenished faster than they are being produced (a genuine long-term positive), and the balance sheet is healthy, so we are not calling this a Sell purely on recent soft share-price momentum. But the recent earnings strength leans heavily on a cyclical refining-margin tailwind rather than the core exploration-and-production business, so we rate it a Hold rather than a name to add to.
positive_para: Profitability metrics are genuinely strong for a state-owned upstream producer: ROE 17.4%, ROCE 16.4%, interest coverage 8.7x, and a moderate D/E of 0.65, all flagged GREEN on balance-sheet and liquidity. The stock trades at an undemanding ~10.5x trailing earnings (value_score 61.2), and consolidated PAT still grew 7% YoY in FY26 to Rs 7,551 cr, with Q4 FY26 alone up 62% YoY on record crude output (decade-high daily production) and a firmer $77.89/bbl realisation. The Reserve Replacement Ratio improved sharply to 1.20x (from 0.94x), meaning the company is adding more reserves than it is producing -- a genuine sign of resource-base health that supports the long production runway. Management is stepping up drilling 35% in FY27 (74->100 wells) and has a credible multi-year plan to lift upstream output from 8.7 to 10-12 MMTOE by FY30, alongside a tripling of NRL's refining capacity (3->9 MMTPA) that should keep contributing a growing, if volatile, profit stream to the consolidated numbers. Dividend policy remains intact (~2.7% trailing yield, Rs 7 interim declared in Q3 FY26).
negative_para: The headline consolidated growth conceals real weakness in the core standalone business: FY26 standalone PAT fell 27% YoY (Rs 6,114cr -> Rs 4,455cr) as crude-segment PBT dropped 29% (Rs 6,073cr -> Rs 4,301cr), and 3-year revenue CAGR is actually negative (-2.0%) -- this is not a story of steady structural growth. Nearly all of the consolidated PAT growth came from NRL's refining margin (GRM $13.43/bbl, PAT +90% YoY), a notoriously cyclical line item that can compress as fast as it expanded, meaning FY26's 'growth' is largely a one-off refining tailwind sitting on top of a shrinking E&P core -- exactly the kind of earnings-quality distortion this process is meant to catch. India's windfall/SAED tax on domestic crude, revised fortnightly against international prices, structurally limits how much of any future oil-price rally OIL's standalone segment actually captures, undercutting the most obvious re-rating catalyst for the stock. Q3 FY26 was a soft quarter (PAT down YoY on weak realisation) showing the earnings line is genuinely lumpy quarter to quarter. The company has also committed $1.8bn (plus a further ~$300mn cost escalation pending Cabinet approval) to the Mozambique LNG (Area 1) project, a foreign asset with a multi-year history of security-driven delays and force majeure for the project's operator -- real capital tied up in an asset with meaningful execution and geopolitical risk that the quant panel cannot see. Price momentum has also been negative (3m -9.0%, 24m -9.3%), consistent with the market discounting the sustainability of the FY26 profit mix.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~10.5x trailing consolidated earnings, the market is pricing OIL as a low-single-digit-growth, cyclical PSU cash generator -- a fair, not rich, multiple given ROE of 17.4% and ROCE of 16.4%. That multiple is roughly consistent with management's own volume guidance (upstream production +4-5%/yr annualised to FY30) plus a modest, uncertain refining-margin contribution from NRL, and does not require heroic assumptions to justify -- but it also is not obviously cheap enough to call a rescue-worthy bargain, because the FY26 earnings base used to compute that 10.5x multiple is flattered by an unusually strong, non-repeatable NRL refining margin while the core crude segment actually shrank. If NRL's GRM normalises lower (refining margins are mean-reverting) even as crude-segment profit stays windfall-tax-capped, forward consolidated EPS could be flat-to-down over the next 1-2 years before the FY30 volume-growth plan starts contributing -- consistent with a Hold, not a re-rating Buy-equivalent case.
